newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati protests election ban.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati protests election ban.

text.p: The ousted leader of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) on Friday marked its 24th anniversary by saying the only legitimate PDI was one under her control.
Megawati Sukarnoputri, daughter of Indonesia's first president Sukarno, told about 300 supporters that her party should be allowed to contest this year's general elections.
"Once again, I want to stress that the only PDI which is entitled to join the general election in 1997 is the one elected for the period of 1993-1998," she said.
"It is not another PDI and also not the PDI under the name of anyone else," she said.

The PDI, one of three political parties allowed to take part in the elections, split after a government-backed congress in Medan, North Sumatra, last June ousted Megawati and elected deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi in her place.
Political analysts said the government supported Megawati's removal because it feared she was becoming too popular.
Surjadi celebrated Friday's anniversary hundreds of miles away with the government-backed faction.
"The internal conflicts of PDI are just being exploited," Surjadi was quoted by the official Antara news agency as telling party members in Tentena, a tourist resort in Central Sulawesi.
Surjadi said he blamed "certain parties" for exploiting the division to gain political recognition. Antara gave no other details.
Last month, the General Election Institute approved a list of Surjadi's candidates -- that excluded all known Megawati supporters -- for the May 29 election.
Last July, Jakarta suffered its worst riots in 20 years after Surjadi backers with police support ousted Megawati followers from PDI headquarters in the city centre.
Her supporters demonstrated in Jakarta and Surabaya on Tuesday demanding the right to run in the elections.
Only the ruling Golkar, Christian-Nationalist PDI and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) are allowed to contest the polls.
All candidates must be approved by a government body which includes military members.
